To those who will be growing your beards for No Shave November, I congratulate you on helping raise awareness for Men's health issues.

The following items are some things I've learned from having a beard for over 5 years to ease you through the process.

  1. Exfoliate - Your skin has been used to scraping off the dead skin almost daily since you've learned to shave. This dosent require anything more than a vigirous scrubbing with warm water while in the shower to eliminate.

  2. Moisturize - If you're used to washing your face every day, stop. If you have a beard, don't wash it every day. This allows for the natural oils to moisturize for you. I only wash my beard once a week, and it doesn't itch or smell, and looks better than a regime of shampos, conditioners, oils, and bs combined.

  3. Go To A Barber - Go to a proper barber, not a stylist. Go to a barber with a beard preferably as they generally serve beer, but also know how to trim a beard. Go after two weeks of growth to clean everything up and make you look clean, continue every 30 days after to ensure the shape you want. Don't try to trim it yourself, you'll fuck it up and your barber will be pissed when you fuck up his work.

  4. Enjoy - Having a beard is a sign of wisdom, patience, and you join a brotherhood that you didn't know existed previously. Take pride in your beard, your body, and your work and you will go far.

Hope this helps all new beard owners, more so during your test run month.
